summary.title: Crafter: A Multi-Agent Harness for Editable Scientific Figure Generation from Diverse Inputs

details: Existing scientific-figure systems each target one figure type from text-only input and emit raster images that cannot be locally revised; because figures are structured compositions of discrete semantic components, generators make localized, high-variance errors (garbled labels, misaligned arrows) that prompt rephrasing or naive retries cannot fix.
Free-text iterative correction accumulates contradictory instructions across rounds, silently degrading faithfulness.

A 'harness' abstraction: a four-role loop (designer -> pluggable executor -> directive verifier -> reviser) around an unmodified generator, whose memory is an evolving structured figure specification updated by typed edits (add layout constraint, ban artifact category, resize named element) rather than appended free text.

Crafter instantiates this for figure generation with five cooperating agents (intent reasoner, plan generator, multi-dimension directive critic, specification refiner, convergence judge), plus diversity-driven parallel exploration of K candidate visual plans and a verify-then-refine loop with best-so-far reversion; all task-specific behavior lives in prompts, so the same architecture covers new figure types and input conditions.

CraftEditor applies the same harness pattern to raster-to-SVG conversion: instruction-driven canvas cleaning (VLM keep/delete plan executed by an image editor) instead of segmentation, element captioning/classification, then iterative SVG skeleton composition refined by a hybrid VLM + programmatic-checker critic.
CraftBench: a 279-sample benchmark covering three figure types and four input conditions with human-annotated conditioning inputs and a per-image referenced VLM-as-judge protocol.
279 samples: text-to-image (179), mask-completion (30), sketch-conditioned (40), key-element composition (30); styles: academic (140), poster (109), infographic (30).
Sources: arXiv figures across 18 subject areas, CVPR highlight/award and ICLR oral/spotlight posters, Lil'Log research blog; 553 candidates filtered to 279.

Seven quality gates (caption keyword filter, VLM content classifier, complexity rubric requiring >=8 named components, claim-alignment check, two QA passes, manual review); every reference-conditioned input accepted only on unanimous agreement of three graduate annotators.

Conditioning inputs built semi-automatically: white-masked semantic regions (~40% area on average), icon-only element skeletons with random displacement, and sketches in three families (hand-drawn, AI-drafted rough, rasterized SVG wireframe).

CraftBench: Gemini 3.5 Flash judge scores candidate and human target independently (no side-by-side, avoiding position bias) on content faithfulness, readability, plus a style-format aspect (t2i) or input-fidelity aspect (conditioned tasks); weighted mean, 0.30 tie band, lenient win-rate over {100,50,0} verdicts; missing generation counts as Human.
PaperBanana-Bench (292 academic methodology figures) scored under its official protocol with Gemini 3.1 Pro.

CraftEditor: 80 held-out Crafter rasters scored 0-10 on seven axes (position, color, text, icon, arrow, style, overall) by a three-VLM ensemble (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, GPT-5.4, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro), mean-aggregated.
Human validation: 60 blind pairwise comparisons by three annotators against the automatic judge.
Image backend: Nano Banana 2 (gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview), also Nano Banana Pro (gemini-3.0-pro-image-preview) to test executor pluggability.
Vision-dependent agents: gemini-3.1-pro-preview (shared by all agentic methods for controlled comparison); language-only agents in Crafter use claude-opus-4-6.

Crafter: K in {1,2,3} adaptive plans from an 11-key style vocabulary, T=3 refinement rounds, early-exit when content accuracy and role conformity exceed 6.5/10 with no artifact detected; critic emits scores on six axes plus issues/suggestions.
CraftEditor: extraction loop T=3, two SVG skeletons at temperatures 0.20/0.45, composition loop T=4 with best-so-far reversion.
Standalone generators: GLM-Image, Qwen-Image (open); GPT-Image-2, Nano Banana 2, Nano Banana Pro (closed), each queried once with the same caption and paper text.
Agentic baselines: PaperBanana and AutoFigure with the same backbone; raster-to-editable baselines: Edit-Banana (SAM-3 + DrawIO) and AutoFigure-Edit (SAM-3 + single-call SVG).

Crafter ablations: remove plan exploration (K=1), corrective layer (free-text revision instead of typed edits), refinement loop (T=1), directive critic; plus K/T scaling sweep and per-figure cost accounting.
CraftEditor ablations: no agentic cleaning (segmentation + background removal fallback), no iterative composition (T=0).

key_findings.finding: The harness layer, not a stronger generator, drives large and uniform gains in scientific figure generation.
key_findings.evidence: Crafter with Nano Banana 2 reaches 50.34 overall on PaperBanana-Bench and 50.20 on CraftBench, beating the strongest agentic baseline PaperBanana by 16.61 and 22.20 points respectively, and exceeding its own standalone backbone by +39.21 and +30.30; it is the only method that improves over its backbone on every quality dimension and every task.

key_findings.finding: Prior agentic pipelines generalize poorly beyond text-to-image academic figures, whereas the prompt-level-adaptable harness does not.
key_findings.evidence: PaperBanana's gain over its backbone shrinks from 22.60 points on PaperBanana-Bench to 8.10 on CraftBench and it falls below its backbone on the sketch task; AutoFigure degrades on both benchmarks; Crafter attains the best score in every column of both benchmarks across its two backbones.

key_findings.finding: All three harness mechanisms contribute independently, with structured typed edits and plan-level diversity mattering most.
key_findings.evidence: On PaperBanana-Bench, removing the corrective layer costs 8.90 points, plan exploration 8.56, refinement loop 5.48, and the directive critic 5.04; K=1 to K=3 alone gives +7.19 and adaptive K adds a further +1.37 (with +3.93 faithfulness over fixed K=3), while T=1 to T=3 gives +5.48.

key_findings.finding: The harness is executor-agnostic, so its benefit is largely independent of the underlying image generator.
key_findings.evidence: Swapping Nano Banana 2 for Nano Banana Pro shifts Crafter's overall score by only 0.34 points on PaperBanana-Bench and 2.10 on CraftBench, with neither backbone dominating uniformly; cost rises from $0.25 to $0.32 per figure (2-3x PaperBanana's $0.11).

key_findings.finding: Applying the same harness pattern to raster-to-SVG conversion yields substantially more faithful editable outputs than one-shot or segmentation-based methods, driven mainly by iterative critic-guided composition.
key_findings.evidence: CraftEditor scores 8.04 overall versus 6.91 (AutoFigure-Edit) and 3.69 (Edit-Banana) under the three-VLM ensemble on 80 rasters, leading on all seven axes; removing iterative composition drops overall by 2.15 while removing agentic cleaning drops it by 0.33 (largest per-axis loss on icons), and ~30% of refinement iterations regress without best-so-far reversion.
